canDo: Can clearly narrate the successive steps of a career path using après avoir/être + past participle, ayant/étant + past participle and une fois + past participle, and explain how each step led to the next.
review: Review day 1’s three layers of past tense (passé composé / imparfait / plus-que-parfait) and day 11’s time expressions (après que + indicative, avant que + subjunctive); today, compress “the earlier action” into a past infinitive or compound participle.
input: Read: a report on career changes, a column arguing for “skills, not diplomas” and a forum post on the VAE — first circle every structure meaning “earlier than”, then reorder the events on a timeline; listen: an interview with a career coach, a segment on “slashers” and an advert for a career-change fair — note “step 1 → step 2” as you listen, paying attention to causes introduced by ayant/après avoir.
output: Write: a formal application letter (≥220 words) to a regional career-change programme’s panel, setting out your experience in time order with at least 4 sequencing structures; speak: a 4-minute monologue on “several careers in one life”, then a debate on “paid leave for retraining”.
checkpoint: Reading + listening accuracy ≥80%; all agreements with après avoir/être + PP correct in the application letter (e.g. après être partie); at least 3 kinds of sequencing structure in a 4-minute monologue without breaking off.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a report on TV5MONDE or RFI’s « Journal en français facile » about a career change or vocational training, write one sentence each with après avoir…, ayant… and une fois… retelling the steps of the person’s path, then record 1 minute of audio about your own (or a relative’s) career path.

questions.why: The headline « trop tard, vraiment ? » challenges the stereotype that “you can’t change careers at fifty”, then uses Odile to show that the road is harder but can succeed with good preparation (« un chemin plus exigeant, qui demande une préparation minutieuse »). B: the text doesn’t discuss recruitment discrimination; C is just a detail of the example.

« à peine un candidat à la reconversion sur dix, alors qu’ils constituent plus d’un quart de la population active »: they are far fewer among career changers than in the workforce. A is the opposite; C: the text gives no failure-rate figures.
The adviser had her « dresser la liste des moments où elle s’était sentie le plus utile », and almost all of them had to do with flowers. Neither A nor B is mentioned.
« dans ma région, beaucoup de fleuristes partent à la retraite sans trouver de repreneur ». B isn’t said; C contradicts the last paragraph, « Elle gagne moins qu’avant ».

« c’est précisément là que l’âge devient un atout »: a fifty-year-old can manage a budget, deal with customers and meet deadlines; all they lack is technique, and « la technique s’apprend ». A is the opposite; C isn’t mentioned.
“A Monday morning in the rain” stands for the hardest, least romantic moments of a job: before changing careers, make sure you would still like it then. A and B are literal misreadings of the image.

The headline « recrutons des compétences, pas des diplômes » and the closing call to « regarder les compétences avant les titres ». A is unrelated to the text’s position; C is explicitly denied: « Je ne plaide pas pour la suppression des diplômes ».

« notre logiciel de tri a automatiquement écarté sa candidature : l’annonce exigeait un diplôme de niveau bac + 5 », and only a colleague’s recommendation got him an interview. B is wrong: he wasn’t shortlisted at first; C is wrong: he was hired in the end.
« On m’objectera que… Certes. Mais… » is a classic concede-and-rebut structure. A: she doesn’t admit a flaw in her argument; B: the text gives no figures.
« mises en situation, exercices pratiques, périodes d’essai bien accompagnées ». A has no basis; C is exactly what she criticises.

« qui restent indispensables dans bien des métiers… Je plaide pour qu’ils cessent d’être un filtre automatique ». B is too absolute; C contradicts « dit peu de chose de ce qu’une personne sait faire aujourd’hui ».

« je voudrais à mon tour raconter ma VAE, puisque plusieurs d’entre vous m’ont posé la question » — sharing her experience to help others. She has already completed the process (A is wrong), and she isn’t complaining (C is wrong).
« je n’avais aucun diplôme au-delà du bac » + « faire reconnaître son expérience ». Neither A nor B is mentioned.
tenir jusqu’au bout = to see it through to the end, i.e. complete the whole process. B is about “starting”; C confuses completing the process with obtaining the full diploma.

The whole interview is about the question « Présentez-vous » and how to tell your career story. A: the focus is the candidate, not the recruiter; C: it is about telling your story aloud, not writing a CV.
« Ils récitent leur CV, poste après poste, sans fil conducteur. » A and B aren’t mentioned.
« partir de la fin, c’est-à-dire du poste visé… on sélectionne les expériences qui y mènent ». C is the opposite of « ce n’est pas un inventaire ».
« montrent qu’une étape en a préparé une autre ». B and C aren’t what she says.
slasheur = someone whose two jobs are joined by a slash, such as « graphiste slash professeur de yoga ».
« elle a négocié un temps partiel avec son employeur », and « Je n’ai pas quitté mon premier métier », so A is wrong; C: she only teaches classes and doesn’t say she opened a school.
« Une partie des slasheurs cumulent les activités par nécessité, faute d’un salaire suffisant ». B and C aren’t mentioned.
« n’ayant pas anticipé cette charge administrative, se découragent ». A contradicts “it took nearly a year to find a balance”; B also involves legal status and contribution systems.
« forum de la reconversion professionnelle », with training organisations, advisers, craftspeople and others exhibiting.
« Nouveauté cette année : des « témoins » ayant eux-mêmes changé de métier animeront une table ronde ». Free entry and the opening hours aren’t presented as new.

V21-01.exZh: In her fifties, Odile went back to sitting on the school benches.

V21-02.exZh: Before changing careers, it’s advisable to do a skills assessment.

V21-03.zh: to be a thing of the past
V21-03.exZh: The days of one job for life are a thing of the past.

V21-04.exZh: In her region, there are plenty of job prospects for florists.

V21-05.exZh: Starting from scratch in a new trade was a lesson in humility for him.

V21-06.zh: to test one’s plan against reality
V21-06.exZh: A work-shadowing placement lets you test your plan against reality.

V21-07.exZh: The manager frowned when he saw I had no diploma.

V21-08.zh: a winding path, a non-linear career
V21-08.exZh: Despite her winding path, she has always followed the same passion.

V21-09.exZh: The company is looking for a technician who is operational from day one.

V21-10.zh: to step back, to take a step back
V21-10.exZh: This year off let me step back and look at my career choices.

V21-11.exZh: Too many recruiters rule candidates out without even meeting them.

V21-12.exZh: Through the VAE, Sabrina had her experience as a department manager recognised.

V21-13.zh: accreditation of prior experience, the VAE
V21-13.exZh: Accreditation of prior experience lets you obtain a diploma without going back to school.

V21-14.exZh: Your introduction lacks a common thread: people can’t follow your choices.

V21-15.exZh: Start from the job you’re aiming for, then work back to your first job.

V21-16.exZh: Too many candidates treat the HR interview as a formality.

V21-17.exZh: After three years in the shop, she was promoted to department manager.

V21-18.zh: to hold several jobs at once
V21-18.exZh: For lack of a sufficient salary, many young people hold several jobs at once.

V21-19.exZh: Léa has to juggle between her office job and her dance classes.

V21-20.exZh: It took her almost a year to find a balance between her two careers.

V21-21.exZh: A former lawyer turned baker will lead the round table at 3 p.m.

V21-22.exZh: She let her plan mature for two years before resigning.

V21-23.exZh: At the end of his placement, he got a job offer.

V21-24.exZh: Without ongoing training, some employees risk being left behind.

V21-25.exZh: In her new job, she had to prove herself during her trial period.

title: Sequence and anteriority
